title: ⚛️ Props Drilling vs Context API — What's the Difference?
excerpt: How do we share that data between components? 🤔
body:
ㅤ 📘 Engineering Notes | From Concepts to Code — Post 15 ㅤ Imagine building a React application where multiple components need access to the logged-in user's information. How do we share that data between components? 🤔 Two common approaches are Props Drilling and the Context API. Let's break them down! 👇 ㅤ 1️⃣ 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗜𝘀 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗽𝘀 𝗗𝗿𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴? 📦 Props drilling happens when we pass data through multiple component levels to reach a deeply nested component. Example: App → Dashboard → Profile → UserInfo Imagine UserInfo needs the user's name. We pass the user data from App through Dashboard and Profile using props. ✅ Simple and explicit data flow ✅ Good for small component trees ⚠️ Can become difficult to maintain when many intermediate components only forward props. ㅤ 2️⃣ 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗜𝘀 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗲𝘅𝘁 𝗔𝗣𝗜? 🌐 React Context allows components to access shared data without passing props through every intermediate level. Example: const UserContext = createContext(null); function UserInfo() { const user = useContext(UserContext); return

{user.name}

; } UserInfo can read the nearest matching context value from a provider above it. ✅ Avoids unnecessary prop drilling ✅ Useful for themes and user information ✅ Simplifies sharing data across components ㅤ 3️⃣ 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗹-𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗹𝗱 𝗘𝘅𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲 🛒 Imagine an e-commerce application. The logged-in user's information is needed in: 👤 Profile 🛒 Shopping Cart 📊 Dashboard ⚙️ Account Settings Instead of passing user data through many component levels, Context can make it available to components that need it. ㅤ 4️⃣ 𝗤𝘂𝗶𝗰𝗸 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗼𝗻 ⚖️ 🔹 Props Drilling • Data passes through components • Explicit data flow • Best for simple component relationships 🔹 Context API • Shares data through a provider • Avoids intermediate prop passing • Useful for widely shared data ㅤ 5️⃣ 𝗪𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝗦𝗵𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱 𝗪𝗲 𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝗘𝗮𝗰𝗵? 🎯 Use props when only a few components need the data. Consider Context when many components at different levels need the same information. ⚠️ Context isn't always better. Frequent context value changes can cause consuming components to re-render. ㅤ 💡 𝗠𝘆 𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗧𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆 Good React architecture isn't about avoiding props completely. It's about choosing the simplest way to share data while keeping components maintainable. 🚀 Use props when they're enough. Use Context when it solves a real problem. ㅤ 💬 Do you prefer using props or Context API for sharing data in React? ㅤ #ReactJS #ReactHooks #SoftwareEngineering #FrontendDevelopment #WebDevelopment
